audit.whatIsWrong: Renekton's Q is called 'Cull of the Meek' three times (early, wants.you[1], wants.foe[2]). The ability is Cull the Meek. Separately, his R is described twice as a knock-up (whys[6], late) — Dominus has no displacement at all.
audit.why: Riot's R text: 'Renekton transforms into the Tyrant form, gaining bonus Health and dealing damage to enemies around him. While in this form, Renekton gains Fury periodically.' Nothing knocks up. A player told to respect an R knock-up will misplay the teamfight entirely.
audit.corrected: Cull the Meek (Q, flat 7s, heals him). Dominus is a bonus-health frontline transform with a damage aura, not an engage knock-up.

audit.why: The Defiant Dance advice is genuinely right in this matchup and worth keeping: Cull the Meek, Ruthless Predator, Slice and Dice and Dominus are all physical damage, so W's physical reduction applies to his entire kit. Unlike the Mordekaiser and Olaf entries in this slice, 'W his combo' is correct here.
audit.corrected: Made the reason explicit rather than leaving it as an unexplained instruction.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ruthless Predator's stun durations, its auto-attack reset, and the anti-heal requirement were all absent.
audit.why: Riot's W text gives exact numbers: 0.75s base, 1.5s at 50+ Fury — twice as long, which is the difference between surviving the follow-up and not. missingInteractions flags both the auto-reset tell (the wind-up, not the cast, is the cue) and needs-antiheal on Cull the Meek.
audit.corrected: 0.75s vs 1.5s stated; wind-up tell and Executioner's Calling timing written into the do's.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows gave the stage to Renekton while their own whys text opened with the opposite word. whys[1], whys[2], whys[3] and whys[6] all literally begin 'Even —', and whys[4] and whys[5] begin 'Irelia owns it —'.
audit.why: The packet chart (Renekton, Skill, Skill, Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Skill) matches the prose word for word, and matches the 50.72% win rate far better than a chart handing Renekton six of seven stages.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-6 flipped in matched full/content pairs; 5/10 for even, 7/10 for Irelia.

audit.whatIsWrong: First-item spike named 'Triforce/bruiser core' in whys[5], spikes[3].text and late while the itemization builds Blade of the Ruined King; and Irelia's passive credited with 'on-hit shred' / 'armor shred' in six places.
audit.why: Ionian Fervor is stacking Attack Speed plus bonus on-hit damage at max stacks — no shred anywhere in Riot's text.
audit.corrected: All renamed to Blade of the Ruined King and Ionian Fervor respectively.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 belong to him — once he has W he builds fury off the wave and his empowered double-strike stuns me, and I only have Q to answer, so I don't walk up to last-hit in his range expecting to win a trade. I farm with Bladesurge off minions and respect that his fury-stacked Cull of the Meek + empowered W chunks me hard. The lane flips at 3: once E is up I can bait his empowered W, and the instant it's down I E-stun, Bladesurge in off the mark, and start stacking my passive armor shred on him.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 belong to him — once he has W he builds fury off the wave and his empowered double-strike stuns me for 1.5s instead of 0.75s, and I only have Q to answer, so I don't walk up to last-hit in his range expecting to win a trade. I farm with Bladesurge off minions and respect that fury-stacked Cull the Meek plus an empowered W chunks me hard and heals him back. The lane flips at 3: once E is up I bait his empowered W, and the instant it's down I E-stun, Bladesurge in off the mark, and stack Ionian Fervor.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a fair fight — my Bladesurge passive comes online and my cooldowns tighten, but he still hits like a truck with fury, so I only commit when his empowered W is spent and I have E up to lock him. Six is my window: Vanguard's Edge walls off his Slice-and-Dice escape, so if he dashes in to all-in me I drop the blade barrier behind him and he can't Dice back out. Channel W to tank the empowered combo, then ramp the extended fight where my on-hit shred wins.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a fair fight — Ionian Fervor comes online and my cooldowns tighten, but he still hits like a truck with fury, so I only commit when his empowered W is spent and I have E up to lock him. His W is an auto reset, so his wind-up is my cue to step out. Six is my window: Vanguard's Edge walls off his Slice and Dice escape, so if he dashes in I drop the barrier behind him and he can't Dice back out. Channel W to eat the combo — all of his damage is physical.

edits.before: My first item (Triforce or bruiser core) is the peak — Bladesurge reset uptime, passive shred, and W's damage-reduction channel make me a lane tyrant while he's item-starved and falling off. This is where I snowball and take plates. Past two items it evens back out: he's a teamfight engage with his R knock-up and I'm a sticky diver, so I convert my lead into towers and objectives rather than greeding the eternal 1v1, which a fed Renekton can still flip with one empowered W stun.
edits.after: My first item (Blade of the Ruined King) is the peak — Bladesurge reset uptime, max Ionian Fervor, and W's physical damage cut make me a lane tyrant while he's item-starved and falling off. This is where I snowball and take plates. Past two items it evens back out: Dominus makes him a durable frontline and I'm a sticky diver, so I convert my lead into towers and objectives rather than greeding the eternal 1v1, which a fed Renekton can still flip with one empowered W stun.

edits.before: Channel W (Defiant Dance) to eat his fury-empowered Ruthless Predator + Cull of the Meek burst, then ramp your passive on-hit shred in the extended fight
edits.after: Channel W (Defiant Dance) to eat his fury-empowered Ruthless Predator and Cull the Meek burst — all of it physical — then ramp Ionian Fervor

edits.before: Trade short with Cull of the Meek lifesteal and Slice-and-Dice out before your Bladesurge passive ramps
edits.after: Trade short with Cull the Meek's heal, then Slice and Dice out before your Ionian Fervor stacks ramp

notes: Renekton's Q was misnamed 'Cull of the Meek' three times, and his R was called a knock-up twice — Dominus is a bonus-health transform with a damage aura and no displacement whatsoever. The level chart handed Renekton six of seven stages while every one of those rows' whys text literally begins with 'Even —' or 'Irelia owns it —'; the packet chart matched the prose and was adopted. Worth noting for the user: this is one of the two matchups in my slice (with Pantheon) where the inherited 'W-block his combo' advice is actually CORRECT, because Renekton's entire kit is physical damage — I kept it and stated the reason instead of stripping it.
